data.title: The landing page leads with situations; mechanism and proof move one click down
data.why: The first outside reader explained the product back correctly from the hero and still did not want it: they did not feel the problem, and the page answered with events, state and a merge proof before naming a day it happens on. Their three questions (context window, compaction or embeddings, a command per decision) were answered nowhere on the page, although the journal holds every answer (DEC-26, DEC-36, the 53 of 53 agent-written decisions). The proof is not weaker for being one click away; the merge illustration and the journal figure now sit on the docs pages that argue them.
data.rejected: Point edits inside the old structure: keeps the order the reviewer stumbled on, and the dense terminals stay; Keep the merge proof as the centre of the page: it is our strongest evidence and answers a question nobody asked first (Probe A: conflicts are real but rare); Staged examples written for the page (KAD-1, ana, a signed cookie): read as a mock-up, and the real journal has better ones
